title: Rail Safety National Law and national regulator (New South Wales)
summary: New South Wales applied the Rail Safety National Law, and the national rail safety regulator began operating on 20 January 2013 for South Australia, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and New South Wales. Rail operators are accredited once, nationally, instead of by each state's regulator.

instruments.title: Rail Safety (Adoption of National Law) Act 2012 (NSW)
instruments.provisions: applies the Rail Safety National Law in New South Wales

commenced.what: Act commenced; national regulator began operating

direction_rationale: A single national law and regulator lets operators that run trains across state borders hold one accreditation and deal with one regulator.

verified.notes: Commencement (20.1.2013) from the NSW Act's legislative history as shown in search results; the NSW legislation site refuses automated requests. The regulator's start date and first jurisdictions are from search results citing ONRSR; for its first years ONRSR regulated New South Wales through a service level agreement with the state regulator.

assessment.summary: One national rail safety law and regulator replaced separate state accreditation, so operators running across borders hold one accreditation and follow one set of rules.

marks.reason: One national accreditation lets operators run services across state borders without separate approvals.
Operators deal with one regulator and one set of safety requirements.
